title: KV index shadow reconciliation and cross-environment fragmentation runtime patch
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Multiple customers running mixed hosted/dedicated/private workloads observed recurring GPU OOMs and long-tail latency spikes tied to a divergence between in-memory KV index structures and the runtime's allocation arenas. The issue manifests as: (1) silent KV index shadow entries that remain reachable but not referenced by session handles, causing gradual memory growth; (2) fragmentation inside the tensor arena that leads to suboptimal compaction and eventual allocation failures under high-concurrency burst patterns. This ticket tracks the investigation, mitigation, and rollout of a fast runtime patch that reconciles KV index state and reduces fragmentation-induced OOMs.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy runtime-1.20 image with KV index debug enabled to a small dedicated cluster
2) Simulate mixed chat+embedding traffic with bursty tail (50k short sessions + periodic long session pins) using load-generator v3.4
3) Observe 'unreferenced' KV-index entries in /proc/runtime_kv_snapshot and increasing slab usage in host metrics
4) Trigger sustained allocation pressure (concurrent 8-token lookups * 400 threads) and watch for GPU OOMs in node logs
5) Confirm that restarting the runtime process temporarily reclaims memory but entries re-accumulate after ~30 minutes
impact_summary: Affected customers experienced intermittent 5-20% error rate increases and instance crashes during peak bursts. Dedicated customers with pinned capacity reported higher incidence due to long-lived sessions; hosted tenants saw elevated latency and some failed tokens. Financial impact: a few customers opened SEV2 escalations and requested immediate mitigation and a stable patch.
mitigation_actions: 1) Deployed a temporary runtime configuration that aggressively trims inactive KV indexes after 60s (from default 15m) to hosted pools
2) Added a circuit-breaker to reject new long-lived session creations when slab usage exceeds 85%
3) Rolled emergency autoscale policy to burst additional dedicated nodes for impacted customers while patch is validated
4) Provided customer-facing status notes and recommended short-term restart schedule where autoscale is not available
root_cause_analysis: Investigation shows a race between session reclamation and the KV index compaction path: under heavy concurrent access, stale shadow index entries were not atomically removed because a deferred compaction task silently failed on a non-fatal allocation path. The failed compaction left small unreachable fragments inside the tensor arena. Over repeated cycles these fragments prevented coalescing, producing effective fragmentation that looked like a leak and ultimately caused allocation failures on the GPU allocator.
proposed_fix: A. Introduce a reconciler pass at async checkpoint boundaries that compares live session handles against KV index roots and performs deterministic removal of shadow entries
B. Harden the compaction task to fall back to an incremental copy-on-write path on allocation failure instead of no-oping
C. Update allocator heuristics to perform a low-overhead slab shuffle when free fraction < 12% to encourage coalescing
D. Add observability: KV-index growth rate, reconciler run times, compaction fallbacks, and fragmentation ratio metrics
test_plan: Unit: new reconciler logic with concurrent handle churn simulated by fakeruntime tests
Integration: reproduce high-concurrency pattern in staging cluster and validate no accumulation of shadow entries over 2h run
Stress: 48h soak with load-generator v3.4 across hosted/dedicated/private configurations at 120% baseline QPS
Canary: deploy to 10% of hosted traffic and one dedicated node pool for 6 hours, monitor OOMs and latency
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR and build runtime-1.21-rc with reconciler enabled behind feature flag
2) Run full test plan in staging and sign-off (SRE+QA+Runtime owners), target duration 48h
3) Canary to hosted 10% and dedicated pool A for 6h, evaluate metrics and customer feedback
4) Gradual ramp to 100% over 12h if no regressions, otherwise roll back to feature-flag-off
5) Post-rollout sweep to backfill reconciler for private/on-prem customers via upgrade notes and optional offline tooling
monitoring_and_metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency by model for impacted routes
